summary.name: Nudge
summary.one_liner: Nudge is a free, open source macOS window manager that snaps windows into halves, quarters, thirds and two-thirds via keyboard shortcuts or drag-to-edge.
use_cases: Snap windows side by side on a Mac
Arrange windows into quarters or thirds with shortcuts
Move windows between multiple monitors quickly
Replace paid Magnet with a free tool
Exclude certain apps from automatic window management
summary.what_it_does: Nudge arranges macOS windows into halves, quarters, thirds and two-thirds positions using 19 keyboard shortcuts that can be remapped in settings. Dragging a window to a screen edge snaps it into place, with a preview overlay showing where it will land. Pressing the same display shortcut twice moves windows across monitors. Users can exclude specific apps from management from the menu bar. It is written in pure Swift and AppKit with no dependencies, and the site says it is under 1MB.
notable: Open source under the MIT license, with no tracking or analytics
Pure Swift and AppKit with zero dependencies, under 1MB footprint
Universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel; installable via Homebrew
caveats: Requires macOS 11 Big Sur or later
Compares itself to Magnet, which the page says costs $9.99; this is the page's claim, not verified
